summary: This CSS file styles a code documentation system with collapsible code snippets, language-specific color variants, and an interactive 'ELI5' (Explain Like I'm Five) feature that displays code with hover-activated explanatory badges and tooltips. The file uses CSS custom properties for theme adaptation, hardcoded colors for language branding, and smooth transitions for interactive elements.

explanations.3: The !important flag forces this background color to always apply, even if other CSS rules try to override it — useful when you want a rule to take absolute priority.
explanations.28: This custom CSS variable stores the rotation angle for the chevron icon; it starts at 0 degrees and changes to 180 degrees when the snippet is expanded.
explanations.35: This selector targets a button that has aria-expanded='true' in its HTML, which tells assistive technology (and this CSS) that the button is in an 'expanded' state.
explanations.39: focus-visible applies styles only when the element is focused by keyboard navigation (not mouse), so users navigating with Tab see a clear outline but mouse users don't get a jarring box.
explanations.52: This rotates the chevron icon by whatever angle is stored in the --chevron-rotation variable — so when the variable changes, the icon smoothly spins.
explanations.61: The transition animates changes to max-height over 0.35 seconds, which creates the smooth expanding/collapsing effect when content becomes visible or hidden.
explanations.73: This selector matches any class name ending with '_icon' (like 'copy_icon' or 'warning_icon'), so one rule applies standardized sizing to all icons at once.
explanations.89: This selector matches any class name starting with 'variant_' (like 'variant_python' or 'variant_docker'), allowing one base rule to apply to all language variants.
explanations.105: The batch language uses a light border color, so the text is set to dark (#2b2b2b) instead of white (#fff) to maintain readable contrast against that light background.
explanations.139: JavaScript uses a bright yellow border, so the text is switched to black (#000) instead of white to keep text readable on the high-contrast yellow background.
explanations.143: JSON variant uses a very dark border color, so the text switches to bright yellow (#ffcc00) for visibility — the opposite of most other languages.
explanations.213: This hardcoded dark gray background ensures the code block is always readable regardless of whether the site is in light or dark mode; the color is intentionally not tied to theme variables.
explanations.224: align-items: flex-start aligns badge/icon elements to the top of each line rather than centering them vertically, so they sit flush with the first line of text.
explanations.230: The hover background uses rgba with 0.04 (4% opacity), which creates a subtle white overlay that appears slightly brightened without looking jarring.
explanations.235: white-space: pre preserves all spaces and line breaks exactly as written in the HTML, preventing the browser from collapsing whitespace like it normally does.
explanations.267: rgba(150, 150, 200, 0.5) creates a semi-transparent lavender border — the 0.5 means 50% opacity, so it blends with whatever color is behind it.
explanations.286: This is a CSS color name (#e8eaf6 is a light lavender) used in the active/hover state of the badge to ensure good contrast against the darker blue background.
explanations.334: :where() is a CSS function that wraps the selector but contributes zero specificity, so this hover rule won't accidentally outrank the button's own :hover rule.
explanations.349: calc(-100% - 8px) positions the tooltip: move up by its own full height plus an extra 8 pixels, so it sits neatly above the badge with a small gap.
explanations.352: min(270px, 90vw) means 'use 270px, but if the viewport is narrower and 90% of it is smaller than 270px, use that instead' — prevents tooltips from overflowing on mobile.
explanations.365: pointer-events: none makes the tooltip unable to be clicked or hovered, so mouse events pass through it to elements underneath — the tooltip just displays information.
explanations.379: The transform: rotate(45deg) makes a small square look like a diamond pointing downward, creating the arrow effect for the tooltip.
explanations.410: font-size: 0.8rem makes this toggle text deliberately smaller and lighter-weight than the main .snippet_summary header to create visual hierarchy.
